title: Cipher Break
intro: Basement Level Two. The Cipher Break wing stores cryptographic puzzles. Each correct answer reveals a digit of the exit code.

puzzles.title: Caesar Cipher
puzzles.prompt:
A Caesar cipher shifts each letter by a fixed number. The plaintext 'HELLO' was encrypted to 'MJQQT'.

What is the shift value used?

variants.prompt:
A Caesar cipher shifts each letter by a fixed number. The plaintext 'HELLO' was encrypted to 'KHOOR'.

What is the shift value used?

hint.text: Count how many positions in the alphabet from H to M (or any plaintext letter to its ciphertext equivalent).

puzzles.teachingPoint: Caesar ciphers are one of the oldest encryption methods — Julius Caesar used a shift of 3. With only 25 possible shifts, a brute-force attack tries all possibilities in seconds. This is why modern encryption uses keys billions of bits long.

puzzles.title: Binary Message
puzzles.prompt:
In binary, each group of 8 bits represents one ASCII character. The message '01001000 01001001' decodes to 'HI'.

How many BYTES are in this message?

variants.prompt:
In binary, each group of 8 bits represents one ASCII character.

How many BITS are needed to encode the 2-character message 'OK'?

hint.text: One byte = 8 bits = one ASCII character. Count the groups of 8.

puzzles.teachingPoint: ASCII uses 7 bits per character (128 values), stored in 8-bit bytes. UTF-8, the modern standard, is backwards-compatible with ASCII but can use 1-4 bytes per character to support every writing system on Earth.

puzzles.title: Password Hashing
puzzles.prompt:
A password hash function produces a fixed-length output regardless of input length. SHA-256 always produces a 256-bit hash.

How many hexadecimal characters does a SHA-256 hash have? (Hint: each hex character represents 4 bits)

variants.prompt:
MD5 produces a 128-bit hash output.

How many hexadecimal characters does an MD5 hash have? (Each hex character represents 4 bits)

hint.text: Divide the bit count by 4 (since each hex digit represents 4 bits: 0-F = 0000-1111).

puzzles.teachingPoint: Hash functions are one-way — you can't reverse them to get the original input. This is why passwords are stored as hashes, not plaintext. When you 'check' a password, the system hashes your input and compares hashes.

puzzles.title: Symmetric vs Asymmetric
puzzles.prompt:
You need to send an encrypted file to someone you've never communicated with before, and you have no way to securely share a secret key in advance.

Which encryption type solves this problem?
choices: Symmetric encryption (same key for encrypt and decrypt)
Asymmetric encryption (public key encrypts, private key decrypts)
No encryption can solve this — you must meet in person first

variants.prompt:
You need to encrypt a large 10GB database backup as fast as possible. You already have a shared secret key with the recipient.

Which encryption type is best for this scenario?
choices: Base64 encode it — that's a form of encryption
Symmetric encryption (AES) — fast with shared key

hint.text: The key distribution problem: how do you share a secret key with someone you can't meet? One type of encryption was invented specifically to solve this.

puzzles.teachingPoint: Asymmetric encryption (RSA, ECC) solves the key distribution problem — anyone can encrypt with your public key, but only you can decrypt with your private key. In practice, HTTPS uses BOTH: asymmetric to exchange a session key, then symmetric (AES) for speed.

puzzles.title: HTTPS Security
puzzles.prompt: When you visit https://example.com, your browser and the server perform a TLS handshake. What is the PRIMARY purpose of this handshake?
choices: To verify the user's identity to the server
To compress the web page for faster loading
To establish an encrypted channel and verify the server's identity
To block malware from being downloaded

variants.prompt: During a TLS handshake, the server sends a digital certificate. What does this certificate primarily prove?
choices: That the server has no malware
That the server is who it claims to be (authenticated identity)
That the server is running the latest software
That the connection speed will be fast

hint.text: TLS (Transport Layer Security) has two jobs: prove the server is legitimate (authentication) and create a secure tunnel (encryption).

puzzles.teachingPoint: The TLS handshake accomplishes three things: (1) authenticates the server via its certificate, (2) negotiates encryption algorithms, and (3) establishes session keys. This all happens in milliseconds before any web page data is sent.
